column1: # .zap/rules.tsv — ZAP passive-scan alert threshold overrides for the `dast`
# CI job (dast-ci-wiring, ADR-021). Format: <rule id><TAB><threshold> where
# threshold is one of IGNORE/INFO/WARN/FAIL. A rule NOT listed here keeps
# ZAP's own default threshold. This file only DOWNGRADES noisy, low-value
# passive alerts for MoneyDiary's context (a token-authed JSON API, no
# browser-rendered HTML/forms) — it never upgrades a rule to FAIL. Real
# findings still surface as WARN in the scan report; slice 1 is advisory
# (`continue-on-error: true` on the `dast` job), so nothing here silently
# hides a signal from the report, it only tunes the threshold column.
# 10015 — Incomplete or No Cache-Control Header: this API returns JSON behind
#   x-api-key + bearer auth; the leak this rule guards against (cached HTML
#   with sensitive data) doesn't apply the same way to a token-authed JSON API.
# 10020 — X-Frame-Options Header Missing: no HTML/iframe surface on this API;
#   clickjacking mitigation belongs to the web client, not the JSON API.
# 10021 — X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing: same JSON-API rationale as
#   10020 above.
# 10096 — Timestamp Disclosure: ISO timestamps (e.g. `expiresAt`) are an
#   intentional, documented part of this API's JSON responses, not a leak.
# 10109 — Modern Web Application: purely informational SPA/JSON-API
#   detection signal, not a finding.
# 10202 — Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens: this API is authenticated via
#   x-api-key + bearer token, not browser cookie+form submission — CSRF
#   tokens are not the applicable mitigation for this transport.
